original.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Help me choose celebration glasses for when our café application gets approved. Please.

original.speaker: B
original.text: We're on the waiting list. I haven't even told my mum.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then just believe it with me here. Which glasses belong in our café?

original.speaker: B
original.text: These two. Mum would insist on a mug.

original.speaker: A
original.text: Choose her mug too. You just pictured our first customer.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: We'll choose the glasses for our cafe. Just two to start; the rest can wait.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: We're still on the waiting list. I haven't even told Mum.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Then we won't buy anything. Show me the ones you'd put on our first table.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: Those two. Mum would want a mug, though.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Find her one. I'll hold these until you've got it.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before we open the landlord's letter, tell me the worst thing it could mean for our shop. Please.

original.speaker: B
original.text: We've only missed one payment.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I know the number. I need you to say the thing I'm counting towards.

original.speaker: B
original.text: We could lose the shop.

original.speaker: A
original.text: And what would that make me, after Dad trusted me with it? Say that bit first too.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: We'll open the landlord's letter together. First, tell me the worst it could mean for Dad's shop.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: We've only missed one payment. Let me read it to you.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: I'll let you read it. But say the worst first, before we know.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: We could lose the shop.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: And what would that make me, after he trusted me with it? Say that too, then you can open it.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before our skating qualifier, can you say the possibility we keep avoiding? Please.

original.speaker: B
original.text: I don't want you carrying that onto the ice.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'm carrying it already. I just need you to say it first.

original.speaker: B
original.text: We might not qualify. I'd still want to skate with you.

original.speaker: A
original.text: Why did I need that second sentence so much? Could you name that fear too?

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: We'll settle our nerves before we leave. Say the worst that could happen at the skating qualifier.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: I don't want you carrying that onto the ice.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: One sentence here, then no more in the car. Say it before we go.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: We might not qualify. Honestly, I'm more worried about your knee.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Then we'll sit. Tell me the worst you're picturing before I choose our warm-up.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Compare the angry letter with the one I sent. Notice the crossing-out. Please.

original.speaker: B
original.text: I appreciate the apology you sent. Why show me the angry version?

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Because 'sorry' took ten minutes. Not sending the rest took all night.

original.speaker: B
original.text: Now I'm tempted to read what you spared me.

original.speaker: A
original.text: Please admire the thickness with it shut. I'd like one night's restraint to survive breakfast.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: I've sealed the angry letter in this envelope. Hold it beside the apology I sent you. Feel the difference.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: I appreciate the apology. I don't need the angry version.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Just hold it a moment. Writing sorry took ten minutes; not sending those six pages took all night.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: Six pages? Now I want to open it.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Keep it shut. You can weigh it in your hand; I want credit for not saying those things.

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I told the committee I couldn't chair another year. Please appreciate what those two sentences took. Please.

original.speaker: B
original.text: Good. Could you stay on until we find someone?

original.speaker: A
original.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I rehearsed in your car until I stopped apologising. That wasn't me advertising a temporary vacancy.

original.speaker: B
original.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

original.speaker: A
original.text: Please don't supply the excuse I spent an hour removing. Could you recognise a refusal I finally managed without one?

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: I'll arrange the handover, but I've told the committee I'm not chairing another year. That took all afternoon in your car.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: Could you stay until we find someone?

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: I'll give you the notes tonight, but don't make me say it again. It took six tries to leave the apology out.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Leave that out. Tell them I said no without an excuse. You heard how hard that was.
